newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian policemen sacked for triggering riot.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian policemen sacked for triggering riot.

text.p: Four Indonesian policeman have been dishonourably discharged for beating up a Moslem teacher in an incident that sparked last month's riot in Tasikmalaya, West Java, the official Antara news agency said on Saturday.

Antara reported that the four policeman were discharged in a ceremony held in Bandung on Friday after they last month beat the teacher and two of his students from a religious boarding school in the Tasikmalaya district.
It identified the men as sergeants Agus Yulianto, Dedi Haerudin and Agus Martadinata, all 24, and Corporal Nursambi, 38.

"Their manhandling of the Moslem teacher and students not only caused harm to the victims but also triggered a riot that claimed human lives and inflicted material damage on the town," West Java police chief Major-General Nana Permana was quoted as saying.

Four people died after an angry mob went on a rampage through Tasikmalaya, destroying a shops, buildings and churches. Reports said every police station in the district suffered some damage, with three police buildings destroyed by fire.
Material damaged had been estimated by authorites at 85 billion rupiah ($36 million).

Antara said the teacher and two students were brought to the police station on December 23 after they disciplined a pupil who was the son of a local police officer. The Kompas daily said Nursambi's son was disciplined after the boy was caught stealing from supermarkets and the Islamic boarding school.

Permana was quoted as saying in the Kompas daily on Saturday that the four policemen still faced court proceedings for their crime, though it was not clear whether they would be tried in a military or civil court.
